relationships.description: The business function reads, creates, updates or deletes the business object as part of its ongoing work, as when Accounting maintains Invoice records.
relationships.evidence: A CRUD matrix, operating procedure or ArchiMate access relationship records that staff working in the function create, read or update instances of that business object.

relationships.description: The parent business function contains the destination sub-function as an integral part of its competency area, so the sub-function has no organizational standing outside it, as with Accounts Payable within Accounting.
relationships.evidence: A functional decomposition or business capability map lists the sub-function as a child node beneath the parent function, with no other parent.

relationships.description: The source business function hands over information, goods or work results to the destination business function, as when Procurement passes approved purchase orders to Accounts Payable.
relationships.evidence: A value-stream diagram, interface agreement or ArchiMate flow relationship documents a named hand-off of a work product from one function's output to the other function's intake.

relationships.description: The business function passes its output or work result into the business process, which takes it as an input to its ordered sequence of activities.
relationships.evidence: A BPMN model or process specification shows the process's start or intermediate input coming from the function, such as a message or data object originating in that functional lane.

relationships.description: The business function supplies the internal behavior through which the externally visible business service is actually delivered to its consumers.
relationships.evidence: A service catalog or service blueprint names the function as the delivering organizational unit or competency behind the service offering.

relationships.description: The business function's ongoing behavior brings about the end state that stakeholders have set as a goal, making the function the means by which that intent is achieved.
relationships.evidence: A strategy or capability-to-goal traceability document maps the goal to the function as its primary contributor, with function objectives that restate the goal.

relationships.description: The business function provides its behavior to support the business role in carrying out its responsibilities, as when an HR function serves the Line Manager role.
relationships.evidence: An internal service-level agreement, RACI chart or operating model names the role as a consumer or beneficiary of the function's output.

relationships.description: Completion or a state change within the business function produces the business event, signaling a named occurrence such as 'month-end close completed' to which other behavior can react.
relationships.evidence: A BPMN or event model shows the event emitted by the function's lane, or a procedure states that the function's action marks the occurrence of that event.

notes: Function realizes Goal is questionable: ArchiMate lets core elements realize requirements and influence goals, so 'supports' or 'influence' fits better. The composes self-relationship has ambiguous direction (whole vs. part as source); it should be documented explicitly. The function serves role relationship is valid but weak, since roles are typically assigned to functions.
